key_insight: A rubric-guided large language model can closely match expert grading of Linux/bash exam answers, but accuracy drops as command complexity increases.
engineering_relevance: This work supports AI-assisted grading pipelines for computing courses, with a taxonomy-based rule for deciding when automation is reliable enough versus when human review is needed.
method: Evaluated four frontier LLMs: GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM.
Compared two prompting styles: minimal baseline vs rubric-enhanced.
Graded 1,200 real student Linux/bash responses using a four-level cognitive taxonomy (L1–L4).
evidence_signal: Gemini 3.0 Pro with rubric prompting achieved the strongest agreement with instructors (ICC(3,1)=0.888, MAE=0.10, Bland-Altman bias=-0.014).
watch_item: Performance declines at higher taxonomy levels, so advanced or ambiguous answers may still require human moderation.
paper_title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach
